QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_24

question.text: Ms. Kavita Joshi is the Key Investment Professional of Arjuna Growth AIF (Cat II). Her sudden resignation triggers the 'key-person event' clause in the PPM. Which of the following is the typical LP-protective mechanism?

answer.text: Automatic wind-up of the fund within 30 days.
Conversion of the Cat II AIF into a Cat III AIF.
Automatic doubling of the management fee to retain remaining team.
Suspension of investment period and capital calls for new investments until a replacement is approved by the LPAC / supermajority of LPs.

explanation.text: The Logic: An industry-standard "key-person event" clause is an LP-protective mechanism: if a designated key investment professional departs or becomes unavailable, the fund's investment period and further capital calls for NEW investments are suspended until the LPAC (or a supermajority of LPs) approves a replacement. Already-made investments are managed through, but no fresh deployment occurs until LPs are satisfied with the replacement. This guards LPs against having their committed capital deployed by an unfamiliar team. The Trap: Automatic 30-day wind-up (A) is extreme and not market-standard. Converting a Cat II AIF into Cat III (B) is not a key-person remedy and would in any event require a fresh SEBI application. Doubling the management fee (C) is plainly anti-LP and not a recognised key-person mechanic. Note: The specific suspension-of-investment-period-and-capital-calls-until-LPAC/supermajority-approval mechanism is not explicitly described in the cited workbook chapter (24 NISM-Series-XIX-D Category I and II Alternative Investment Fund Managers Certification Examination_January 2026.pdf, pp. 77, 83-84, 137, 182, 184, 191, 244, 248-249, 283, 327-328, 366, 397), which supports key-team disclosure and key-person risk but not the suspension mechanism. The framing above is general industry/PPM practice.
